title: LatticeMind: A Conflict-Aware Memory Primitive for Multi-Agent Systems
reason: 核心贡献是面向多智能体的持久化共享记忆：在写入时用符号检查和选择性 LLM 裁决处理冲突，记录条目状态与来源，供后续智能体读取。文中给出更新规则和伪代码；单骨干、去除来源标签提示的对照评测中，准确率为 0.965，对照组最高为 0.525。消融支持裁决器的作用，但检查器的差异未达常用显著性阈值（p=0.07）。等预算的软件状态跟踪和混合的规划结果界定了适用范围；协调分支未获验证。
abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems often fail not for lack of candidate answers, but because they have no persistent mechanism for deciding which incompatible claim should currently be trusted. Majority vote, debate, and judge-based selection choose an output without recording which claim wins, which is contested, or why a later update supersedes it. We present LatticeMind, a conflict-aware structured memory that handles contradiction at write time. It maintains explicit item status, applies cheap symbolic conflict checks, and routes the flagged cases to an LLM reconciler. On a label-blind ConflictBank evaluation that removes source-name hints, over a uniform draw of 200 examples from the full benchmark pool, LatticeMind reaches 0.965 accuracy versus 0.525 for the strongest baseline, with every gap significant at p<10^{-24} by paired McNemar test. Ablations show that removing the checker or the reconciler costs 12 to 14 points. Our claims are scoped to credibility conflicts, where one claim should defeat another: the coordination branch of the design is a safety override that we do not validate empirically, and all prompt-based comparisons are conditioned on a single backbone. On three secondary planning benchmarks and one synthetic scheduling diagnostic the picture is mixed: LatticeMind beats naive merge on three of four, but does not replace deliberation methods on tasks rewarding iterative search.
evidence: We present LatticeMind, a conflict-aware structured memory that handles contradiction at write time.
result: LatticeMind reaches 0.965 accuracy versus 0.525 for the strongest baseline
